questions.explain: The chapter names three: the threshold model (a fixed boundary assumes the same metric always means the same thing, ignoring context), alert fatigue (noise teaches operators to ignore notifications), and correlation failure (twenty alerts for one blocking chain, with no system connecting the dots).
options: High licensing cost, lack of PowerShell integration, and vendor lock-in

Static thresholds assume a fixed boundary always means the same thing regardless of context; alert fatigue teaches operators to ignore pages; and correlation fails when twenty alerts are all downstream effects of one blocking chain
Prometheus cannot scrape SQL Server, Grafana has no alerting, and Extended Events XML is deprecated
Alert rules cannot reference multiple metrics, dashboards are too slow, and logs are stored in incompatible formats
questions.q: Which three failure modes does the chapter identify in classical threshold-based monitoring?

questions.explain: The dual-write pattern pushes numeric metrics to Prometheus for the time-series path while pushing semantic snapshot descriptions, embeddings, and metrics_json to a native VECTOR column in SQL Server 2025 for AI retrieval.
options: All metrics are duplicated across two Prometheus servers for high availability
Numeric metrics go to Prometheus while semantic health snapshots and embeddings are stored in SQL Server's native VECTOR(1536) column for AI retrieval
Prometheus and Grafana each write to the same SQL Server table simultaneously
The exporter writes metrics once and Prometheus pulls a second copy from SQL Server
questions.q: What is the 'dual-write' architecture for the metrics pipeline that AI can actually use?

questions.explain: The schema uses embedding VECTOR(1536), a CREATE VECTOR INDEX ... WITH (METRIC='cosine') DiskANN index, and VECTOR_DISTANCE('cosine', ...) to retrieve the most similar historical snapshots — the retrieval step of RAG applied to operations.
options: dbo.db_health_snapshots uses a VECTOR(1536) column with a DiskANN index created via CREATE VECTOR INDEX ... WITH (METRIC = 'cosine'), queried with VECTOR_DISTANCE
VECTOR columns require the spatial indexes from the geography type, so snapshots are stored as GEOGRAPHY
Embeddings are stored as NVARCHAR(MAX) JSON and compared with LIKE clauses
SQL Server 2025 removed VECTOR support, so the chapter stores embeddings in a VARBINARY hash
questions.q: How does the chapter store and query health-snapshot embeddings for similarity search in SQL Server?

questions.explain: Without deduplication, an anomaly persisting for ten minutes would generate dozens of PagerDuty incidents and pages — the chapter explicitly says the dedup_key exists to avoid recreating the alert fatigue problem it is trying to solve.
options: To encrypt the PagerDuty payload before transmission over HTTPS
To prevent PagerDuty from creating dozens of duplicate incidents when the same anomaly persists across multiple alert evaluations
To rate-limit the Slack webhook so messages arrive no faster than one per minute
To hash the narrative text so it fits within PagerDuty's 1024-character summary limit
questions.q: Why does the enriched-alert function compute a dedup_key from the snapshot timestamp when triggering PagerDuty?

questions.explain: The Isolation Forest is retrained weekly on a rolling 30-day window, and the training query excludes known incident windows (incident_id IS NULL) so a prolonged incident does not corrupt the baseline with anomalous data.
options: It is trained once on the first week of data and never retrained
It retrains hourly on all available data including incident windows for maximum coverage
It retrains monthly on a full year of snapshots to smooth out seasonality
It is retrained weekly on a rolling 30-day window that excludes snapshots tagged with incident_id IS NOT NULL, so prolonged incidents do not corrupt the baseline
questions.q: How is the Isolation Forest anomaly model trained and maintained in the monitoring loop?
